What's amazing about Tarbosaurus?

Asia's tyrant, Tarbosaurus, was a dinosaur like a cousin of Tyrannosaurus. Many of its fossils have been found in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia.

content.text:
Nature and science facts about Tarbosaurus

Tarbosaurus lived in Asia (Mongolia) in the late Cretaceous, about 70 million years ago. It was roughly 10–12 m long and weighed 4–5 tons. Its skull was narrower, longer, and lighter than T. rex's, and it had around 60 serrated teeth. Its front arms were even smaller than T. rex's, and its side-facing eyes gave it a wide field of view. Its fossils mostly come from Mongolia's Gobi Desert.

Points worth exploring together

Point out things like its Asian (Mongolian) origin, narrow skull, tiny front arms, and how it differs from T. rex. It's fun to talk together about "What's different between Tarbosaurus and Tyrannosaurus?"

Parent guide — how to spark curiosity

Find Mongolia on a map and show them "This is where the fossils were found." Placing photos of T. rex side by side to spot the differences in skull shape makes for a fun game, too.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Where did Tarbosaurus live?
A. It lived in Asia (Mongolia) about 70 million years ago. Many fossils are found in the Gobi Desert.

Q. How is it different from Tyrannosaurus?
A. Its skull was narrower, longer, and lighter, and its front arms were smaller. It also lived in Asia.

Q. How can we enjoy this at home?
A. Find Mongolia on a map and compare skull shapes with T. rex.
